Steering knuckle support and wheel-hub prose

source_title: Колесное шасси МАЗ-543 и его модификации. Техническое описание и инструкция по эксплуатации, 3rd edition 1977

observations.claim: The steered-wheel drive chain comprises a central-reducer halfshaft, an open two-joint halfshaft Cardan with needle-bearing crosses, and a separate outer halfshaft with a constant-velocity joint. The latter has a cage carrying two crosses, pin-connected inner/outer members, and an input flange supported by two ball bearings in the knuckle support.
observations.limit: The two external Cardan joints and the distinct in-knuckle CV joint must not be conflated. Figure proportions do not provide manufacturing dimensions or prove the retained reconstruction matches these parts.

observations.claim: The steering knuckle has two trunnions forming the steering axis; its support is carried on two needle bearings with an upper thrust ball bearing. The support has bosses for suspension-arm attachments. The constant-velocity joint is inside the knuckle.
observations.limit: Topology described by the primary text; no exact source/model feature correspondence or hardpoint coordinates established in this reading.

observations.claim: The wheel hub is supported on two tapered roller bearings. The drum is located on the inner centering land and bolted to the hub; its working surface is machined with that hub assembly.
observations.limit: The brake drum belongs to the hub assembly geometrically; the reading does not identify current model objects or prove brake mechanism closure.

observations.claim: The drawing explicitly dimensions the vertical lower-arm head-center separation as 136 plus5 mm.
observations.limit: This is a shown dimension, not pixel scaling of the remaining linkage; no complete lengths, joints, tolerances or hardpoint set is inferred from drawing proportions.

observations.claim: For torsion-bar installation/replacement, front and rear lower-arm head centers must have vertical separation136–141mm (543M138–143mm), and support bolts are screwed against the upper arms and locked.
observations.limit: Installation state, not neutral/unloaded/loaded road height or a prescribed wheel travel.

observations.claim: Correctly installed torsion bars should leave the upper suspension arms close to horizontal with the chassis fully loaded. Permanent torsion set may alter steered-wheel camber and reduce the support-bolt gap.
observations.limit: No numerical tolerance for close to horizontal, no specific qualified model load/pressure state, and no full force/compliance model established.

camber_sign_status: No explicit wheel-plane sign convention or camber tolerance established in these pages; prior nominal1degree magnitude still applies only to steered wheels.
modeling_consequence: Compare actual current lower/upper arm angles and head-center z differences at every candidate; keep installation and fully-loaded constraints separate. Do not assign source correctness to a reachable inward1degree pose, force an unreachable outward pose, move fixed axes, or infer dimensions from drawing scale. Preserve the distinction between halfshaft Cardan and in-knuckle CV joint; a straight-ahead external-flange axis correction does not validate steering or constant-velocity internals.
